That's a creative idea, there are several technical challenges:
What MIGHT work:
Chrome extensions CAN detect media button events (play/pause, next, previous) from Bluetooth headphones
These events are passed through to Chrome as keyboard-equivalent events
You could theoretically trigger actions with these buttons
Major limitations:
Screen-off issue: When your Chromebook screen is off, Chrome and its extensions are typically suspended or severely throttled. Chrome extensions generally don't run when the device is in sleep mode. Microphone permissions: Chrome extensions need explicit permission to access the microphone, and this usually requires:
The browser to be active (not suspended)
User consent through a permission prompt
The tab/extension to remain active
Background processing: Chrome OS aggressively manages power, so background audio recording while the screen is off is intentionally restricted for privacy and battery reasons. More realistic approach:
Use the media buttons while the screen is ON but dimmed
Create a Chrome extension that:
Listens for media button events
Triggers microphone recording
Keeps the screen at minimum brightness
Or use an Android app like "Easy Voice Recorder" which might handle sleep states better
Privacy note: Chrome OS has built-in protections against apps secretly recording audio, especially when the device appears to be off. This is by design for user security.
